record.paper_title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigenfunction Decompositions of Hill Operators: Open Questions
record.original_question: Let W = { z : C(z) = ∞ } be the exceptional set associated with the comparison inequality ∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| <= C(z) * |∑_{x ∈ X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)| from the preceding question. Determine the structure of this exceptional set W inside C^m.

evidence.quote: Question 5. Is it true that (19) holds for almost all {V } = z ∈ C^m. The structure of the exceptional set W = {z : C(z) = ∞} is of special interest also.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $m \geq 1$ and $n \geq 1$. For a vector $z = (V_1, \dots, V_m) \in \mathbb{C}^m$ regarded as parameters of a trigonometric polynomial potential, let $F_m$ denote the associated combinatorial datum and let $X_n^+(F_m)$ denote the finite set of admissible configurations of size $n$ arising from the eigenfunction-decomposition combinatorics of the corresponding Hill operator (so that each $x \in X_n^+(F_m)$ contributes a complex weight $h(x) = h(x; z)$ depending polynomially on the coordinates of $z$).

For $z \in \mathbb{C}^m$, define
$$C(z) := \sup_{n \geq 1} \sup_{h} \frac{\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)|}{\bigl|\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)\bigr|},$$
where the inner supremum is taken over the admissible weight functions $h$ from the spectral problem (with the convention that the ratio is $0$ when both numerator and denominator vanish, and $\infty$ when only the denominator vanishes). Define the exceptional set
$$W := \{ z \in \mathbb{C}^m : C(z) = \infty \}.$$

Determine the structure of $W$ as a subset of $\mathbb{C}^m$: in particular, decide whether $W$ has Lebesgue measure zero (so the comparison inequality $\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} |h(x)| \leq C(z) \bigl|\sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x)\bigr|$ holds for almost every $z \in \mathbb{C}^m$), and describe $W$ geometrically (e.g., as a countable union of analytic subvarieties, or otherwise).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned the original problem source and related works by Djakov–Mityagin on convergence/divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with trigonometric polynomial potentials, plus a follow-up paper "On a Combinatorial Identity of Djakov and Mityagin." None of the visible results explicitly resolves the structural description of the exceptional set $W = \{z : C(z) = \infty\}$ in $\mathbb{C}^m$. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial Identities Related to Eigen-Function Decompositions of Hill operators: Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions formulated by Djakov and Mityagin concerning combinatorial identities arising in spectral decompositions of Hill operators.
status_evidence.claim: The exceptional-set structure question is posed as an open question alongside the almost-everywhere validity of the comparison inequality.

status_evidence.title: On a Combinatorial Identity of Djakov and Mityagin
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work giving a combinatorial proof of one of the identities of Djakov and Mityagin.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses related combinatorial identities but does not appear to resolve the structure of W.

status_evidence.title: Divergence of spectral decompositions of Hill operators with two exponential term potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Djakov–Mityagin paper on divergence cases for trigonometric/exponential potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Related divergence results exist but do not give a full description of the exceptional set in $\mathbb{C}^m$.
